experiment: Phase 4 Module 2 - Hard-Negative Cascade Classifier on top of Plan A

method.base: Plan A (Phase 2.5) predictions on HERIDAL val
method.data_collection: Plan A SAHI inference on HERIDAL train; match each pred vs GT by IoU; IoU>=0.5 -> person, IoU<0.1 -> not_person, in between -> drop
method.classifier: MobileNetV3-Small (timm pretrained), 64x64 crops with 1.5x bbox padding
method.inference: drop bbox if person_prob < 0.5; multiply Plan A score by person_prob

conclusion: Cascade classifier is neutral on overall mAP metrics but drops AP_small by 11.5 points absolute. The 0.5 threshold filters out 38.9% of predictions, and a disproportionate fraction of those drops are small-scale TPs that the MobileNetV3-Small classifier could not confidently identify.
diagnosis_hypotheses: 64x64 input crops are too small for the classifier to learn person-vs-distractor discrimination at the small-person scale (~30 px person becomes ~45 px in the 1.5x padded crop, then downsampled to 64). Signal-to-noise too low.
Class-balanced sampling during training may have over-weighted the smaller hard-negative class, pushing decision boundary inward
Threshold 0.5 is too strict; threshold 0.3-0.4 may keep more small-person TPs at modest precision cost
Training data (Plan A predictions on train) may have insufficient small-person TPs to learn small-scale features
future_work: Sweep CASCADE_THRESHOLD in {0.2, 0.3, 0.4, 0.5} to find precision/recall sweet spot
Use larger crop size (128x128) to preserve more detail at small-person scale
Train scale-conditional classifier (small/medium/large heads or scale-aware embedding)
Try ResNet18 instead of MobileNetV3-Small - larger receptive field may help
Re-evaluate as score re-weighter only (multiply but never drop), not a hard filter
